qualification: Published v0.4.10 -> v0.4.11 Docker evaluation upgrade with both releases' published bundles, images and launchers, on one Linux arm64 Docker engine, from a fresh v0.4.10 installation (portable lineage 0011-0019). The pair runs 0020 and 0021, so the migrator opens the transition 0019..0021 (ADR-0156 amendment 1). Logical backup on the same host. Not the published lineage, not off-host recovery, not Kubernetes.

outcome.clean_upgrade: passed: 235 s receipt, 233 s readiness gap, 0019 -> 0021 in 0.3 s; the catalogue's constraint, column, index, trigger, policy, function and relation names changed by exactly those 0020 and 0021 create or replace
outcome.incompatible_releases: passed: v0.4.10's gateway, worker, read-only check and migrator each refused stamped 0021 without writes
outcome.no_pending_migration_with_writers_connec: passed: v0.4.11 migrate reported 0021 -> 0021 in 0.3 s and refreshed only the stamp's updated_at
outcome.interrupted_stamp: passed: over a hand-set 0019..0021 marker and the 0021 ledger, both releases' gateway and worker refused, and v0.4.11 migrate returned the marker to 0021 and changed nothing else but updated_at
outcome.upgrade_with_injections: passed: a writer-drain refusal left the marker at 0019; a lock refusal in 0020 left 0019..0021 over the 0019 ledger; one in 0021 left 0019..0021 over the 0020 ledger. Both releases' workers and v0.4.10's check and migrator refused each open state, the gateways stopped earlier at their OIDC diagnostic, and the same command then completed
outcome.installed_launcher_against_open_transiti: passed: v0.4.10's up refused at migrate and wrote nothing
outcome.gateway_against_open_transition: passed: with Keycloak running, both releases' gateways refused 0019..0021 over the 0020 ledger at their epoch stage
outcome.rollback_by_restore: passed four times with the v0.4.10 bundle: the pristine pre-upgrade set twice, and the upgrade's own set after each mid-transition refusal
outcome.launcher_direction: known limitation confirmed: after the refused writer drain the launcher said the schema change began, but the marker stayed 0019 and v0.4.10's read-only check accepted the database
outcome.read_only_check_exit: finding: v0.4.11's migration-check exits 0 for an open transition over the 0019 ledger and 1 over the 0020 or 0021 ledger, though every message directs to this image's migrate

digest_method: snapshot.py: one REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY transaction as the bundled superuser over the local socket, hashing every row of every table (with the pre-upgrade column list, so added columns leave existing rows' digests unchanged), the SQLx ledger, schema_metadata, public views, extensions, each tenant's audit chain and audit prefix, and the catalogue: every public constraint and index definition, column definition, trigger, row-level security policy, function (definition digest, owner, SECURITY DEFINER, settings and ACL) and relation (kind, owner, ACL and row-level security flags). expected.py checks a comparison's catalogue change against the object names each migration creates or replaces, listed by hand from its SQL; it checks names, not definitions. A comparison block leaves out tables_added when none were added, catalogue when it is identical, and catalogue_expected when no migration was expected

deviations: expected.py first compared the tables added since the frozen column list, not those added between the two snapshots, so phase-b.log shows a false 'exit=1' for the no-pending migrate. compare.py now reports the tables added and removed between the two snapshots, and the phase A and B comparisons were rerun from the retained snapshots; every result in this record uses the corrected tools.

After phase D, phase-f.sh gained its own pre-mid baseline, because the restored installation carries the flattened constraint that pre-0410 does not. readiness.sh, which summarises the samples, was written after the clean run.
The trailing stamp was set by hand (UPDATE public.schema_metadata SET migration_head = '0019..0021') rather than produced by a failed stamp write.
expected.py exited 1 for both restores of the pristine set, on the flattened capture_batches_retry_check alone.
During the clean upgrade, one read-only command ran in the drill engine: sha256sum of the two launchers, the environment.json image lists and the engine's version.
The gateway probes after attempts 2 and 3 never reached the database (Keycloak stopped); gateway_against_open_transition was added after the main run to observe them.
